eventos.descripcion: Carlos de Anjou, backed by the papacy, defeats and kills Manfredo in Benevento. The Hohenstaufen monarchy loses effective control of Sicily and Naples.
Conradino invades Italy to recover his family's inheritance, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou is left as the owner of the old Hohenstaufen kingdom.
After years of war, the Sicians hold up Federico, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line opposite the Andean Naples.

The peace of Caltabelletta recognizes Frederick on the island and the Anjou on mainland. The old Sicilian monarchy remains politically broken between Trinacria and the kingdom that historiography will call Naples.

Alfonso V. of Aragon defeates the angevine resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since the Visperas, an same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the mainland kingdom, though the crowns have separate identities.

eventos.titulo: The inheritance of Alfonso once again secures
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to his brother John II while Naples remains for his son Fernando. The personal union does not become a stable fusion of the crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Fernando the Catholic agree to share with themselves the kingdom of Federico I. The cooperation lasts for little: the challenges about the boundaries of partition turn old allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Grand Captain challenges the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms strengthens the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance that was born from the 1500 division was definitely broken in favor of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Fernando gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Fernando the Catholic as King of Naples and Trinacria. The two parts of the old Sicilian monarchy share again sovereign, but will continue to be administered as different kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

In Mesina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetian, pontificas, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

Pius V accompanies the coalition with public pleas, blesses the company and sends Don Juan a pontifical banner. The Catholic memory will then associate the victory to the prayers and the Rosary; the tradition that the Pope knew the triumph before receiving the news belongs to devotional tradition, not to a fact that can be demonstrated by itself.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.

In the center, the Royal Galera of Don Juan and the Sultana of Ali Bajá are stuck in a struggle of approaches, archauces and successive reinforcements. The fall of Ali Bajá and the take of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic core of victory.

eventos.titulo: The wings almost changed the result.
eventos.descripcion: Barbarigo is morally injured in the Christian left wing. At the opposite end, Uluç Ali takes advantage of the open space during Doria's maneuver and hits several League galleys. The reservation of Alvaro de Bazan comes to close the gap, while Uluç Ali manages to withdraw with part of his ships.

Miguel de Cervantes fights as a soldier in the Marquesa galley. He is injured during the day and loses the use of his left hand, an experience he will remember throughout his life as one of the great occasions of his time.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to leave his Sicilian purport at Anagni, but the Sicilian did not accept to come back to Angevin rule. They chose his brother Federico and forced the Casa de Barcelona to divide about his future.

Caltabellotta had been planning to put up with his life and a later solution to the Anjou. To associate Peter with his throne, the island house defended his own hereditary transmission. The peace of 1302 had been closed.

eventos.titulo: The death of his heir leaves his crown to a granddaughter
eventos.descripcion: Carlos de Calabria died before Roberto. Juana inherited his crown and had to uphold his authority with his own family branches. The murder of Andres de Anjou later triggered the invasions of Luis of Hungary.

eventos.titulo: A new peace redefines the two Sicilia
eventos.descripcion: The papal mediation gave a new framework to Federico's recognition as King of Trinacria with obligations to Juana. The names of Sicily and Trinacria expressed rights discussed as well as a geographical separation.
Juana had chosen Louis of Anjou as heir, but Carlos of Durazzo conquered the kingdom. His death and that of Juana left the next generation a war between Anjou and Durazzo, not a peaceful succession.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to put their arms at the Barons. The Queen's hereditary legitimacy was insufficient without his military capacity. The island's government again closely linked with the Aragon's Crown.

The massacre of protesters at Wassy by duke de Guisa's men accelerates his uprising led by Luis de Condé and opens the first of the French Religious Wars.

name: Sweden
summary: The Swedish monarchy alternated between election, inheritance and regency both within and outside the Scandinavian unions. Bjälbo, Mecklenburg, the kings of Kalmar and the Vasa do not form an uninterrupted sequence: internal resistance and changes of dynasty are essential to understanding it.

name: Guelders
summary: Guelders was raised from a county to a duchy in 1339 under Reinald II. The conflict between his sons Reinald III and Edward brought deposition and restoration rather than a linear succession by death. Their deaths in 1371 opened a dispute between Matilda and the line of Maria, whose son William brought the duchy to the House of Jülich. In 1423 Arnold of Egmond asserted his rights through Joanna of Jülich and Maria van Arkel. The later struggle between Arnold and his son Adolf allowed Charles the Bold to intervene. Charles of Egmond’s recovery of the duchy shows that the Burgundian acquisition was not final.

translatedSource.resumen: Guelders was raised from a county to a duchy in 1339 under Reinald II. The conflict between his sons Reinald III and Edward brought deposition and restoration rather than a linear succession by death. Their deaths in 1371 opened a dispute between Matilda and the line of Maria, whose son William brought the duchy to the House of Jülich. In 1423 Arnold of Egmond asserted his rights through Joanna of Jülich and Maria van Arkel. The later struggle between Arnold and his son Adolf allowed Charles the Bold to intervene. Charles of Egmond’s recovery of the duchy shows that the Burgundian acquisition was not final.

Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of the Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the continuity Habsburg
eventos.descripcion: In the course of the Austrian War of Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Carlos Alberto obtained the imperial crown and showed that dignity remained elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurates the Habsburgo-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Mary Teresa and creates the Habsburgo-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, tried to reform the Habsburg domains quickly, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

name: Norway
summary: The Norwegian monarchy passed from the House of Sverre into several personal unions. Transmission through Ingeborg of Norway and the marriage of Haakon VI to Margaret explain the connections with Sweden and Denmark. At every transition, inheritance of the title must be distinguished from the condition of Norwegian institutions.

people.FRED5DEN: King of Denmark and Norway between 1746 and 1766. His reign, largely ruled by ministers such as Bernstorff and Moltke, remained neutral and favored trade and the arts.
people.CHRISTIAN7DEN: King of Denmark and Norway since 1766, suffering from a serious mental illness. The power was exercised by others: Struensee until 1772 and, since 1784, his son, the future Frederick VI.
people.FRED6DEN: He exercised the regency for years before succeeding Christian VII. The Napoleonic Wars ended with the loss of Norway in 1814. The cession agreed at Kiel was followed by a Norwegian constitutional movement, a war and a new agreement.
people.MARGARETSCOTNOR: Princess of the House of Dunkeld. Their life was connected with Scotland, Norway.
people.ERIK2NORWAY: Son of Magnus VI and Ingeborg of Denmark. His marriage to Margarita of Scotland made him the father of the so-called Norwegian Dowel, a Scottish heiress who died before he settled in the kingdom. When Erik died without a surviving male son, his brother Haakon V.
people.MAIDNORWAY: Alexander III's granddaughter and recognized heiress of the Scottish crown. He died in 1290 during the trip to Scotland, triggering the succession dispute known as the Great Cause.
people.MARGDINESCOCIA: Consort of the House of Oldenburg. Their life was connected with Denmark, Norway, Scotland.
people.HAAKON4NOR: His reign closed the long stage of Norwegian civil wars and strengthened the monarchy. The expansion to Iceland and Greenland expanded its Atlantic horizon. His son Magnus VI continued the dynasty; on that line they descend Haakon V, Ingeborg of Norway and the kings that gathered Norway and Sweden.
people.MARGRETESKULE: Margarita, daughter of Duke Skule Bårdsson, married Haakon IV. The alliance did not prevent the subsequent confrontation between her father and her husband. She was the mother of Magnus VI: her offspring links the Norwegian medieval consolidation with the Scandinavian unions of the 14th century.
people.MAGNUS6NOR: Known as the Legislator for the compilation of a common law for Norway. His marriage to Ingeborg from Denmark connected the neighbouring royal houses. His sons Erik II and Haakon V reigned in a row; both their daughters took the succession to Scotland and Sweden.
people.INGEBORGERIKNOR: Daughter of Erik IV of Denmark and wife of Magnus VI of Norway. She was the mother of the kings Erik II and Haakon V. After Magnus's death he participated in the government during the Erik minority, in a context of tensions between the crown, the aristocracy and the Church.
people.HAAKON5NOR: He succeeded his brother Eric II. His daughter Ingeborg married the Swedish prince Eric Magnusson; their son Magnus inherited Norway in 1319. This transmission through the female line allowed the Norwegian crown and the Swedish election to converge on the same child.
people.EUFEMIARUGENNOR: Wife of Haakon V and mother of Ingeborg of Norway. Its cut is associated with the dissemination of chalereresque romances translated into Swedish, the so-called Eufemiavisor.
people.OLAF2NORD: Son of Margarita and Haakon VI. He was elected king of Denmark as a child and inherited Norway upon the death of his father. His mother led the government. Olaf's death without descent in 1387 forced him to seek another successor solution and opened the way to the recognition of Margarita and Erik of Pomerania.
people.PHILIPPAENGLAND: Daughter of Henry IV of England and Mary of Bohun. His marriage to Erik of Pomerania connected the monarchy of Lancaster with Kalmar.

eventos.titulo: The Union of Lublin creates the Community
eventos.descripcion: Poland and Lithuania move from a dynastic union to a closer political community. The new structure will survive the male extinction of the Jagellones and will make a common elected monarchy possible.
Following the death without heirs of Segismundo II Augusto, the nobility chose Henry of Valois and set his true power with his final limits through his Henricians.

eventos.titulo: Ana Jagellón and Stephen Báthory share the crown
eventos.descripcion: The choice of Stephen Báthory with Ana Jagellón shows that the dynastic legitimacy still matters, but it is no longer enough on its own: the crown depends on the choice of nobility.

eventos.titulo: A Vasa is elected King of Poland
eventos.descripcion: Segismundo III Vasa arrives at the Polish-Lithuanian crown as grandson of Segismundo I and Swedish prince. The election opens up a stage at which the Communidad intersects directly with the dynastic struggles of the Baltic.
After decades of wars and crises, John II Casimir abandons his throne. Nobility can re-choose from scratch and leapt for a candidate born within his own Commonwealth.

eventos.titulo: The Battle and Relief of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, habeburgic and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman site of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens up a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Augusto the Strong gets the crown
eventos.descripcion: The election of Saxony becomes Catholicism and is able to be elected king. Poland - Lithuania is personally united with Saxony and its choice makes the crown a European issue.
Estanislao Leszczyński and Augusto III are proclaimed by rival factions. The dispute leads to a European war and shows how far the neighbouring powers can condition electoral freedom.

eventos.titulo: The Last King of the Republic
eventos.descripcion: Estanislao Augusto poniatowski is elected king with a reformist program but under Russia's decisive shadow. The tension between noble freedom, reform and outside intervention enters its final phase.

eventos.titulo: The May 3 Constitution tries to change the system
eventos.descripcion: The new constitution eliminates the liberum veto and replaces the elective monarchy with an hereditary succession envisaged in the house of Saxony. It is the most ambitious attempt to reform the Republic from within.

eventos.titulo: The third partition ends with the Commonwealth
eventos.descripcion: The third partition erases the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the political map and forces Estanislao Augusto to abdicate. The chosen crown experiment concludes under pressure from the neighbouring monarchies.
Luis de Condé dies after the battle of Jarnac. Gaspar de Coligny remains as the leading military boss of the town while Duke of Anjou, future Henry III, gain prestige in the Catholic field.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Paris RetiN up for the League
eventos.descripcion: The Day of Barricades forces Henry III to leave Paris and shows that the League and Henry of Guisa can directly challenge the king in his own capital.

eventos.titulo: Henry III killed the Duke of Guisa
eventos.descripcion: Fearing to lose control of the monarchy, Henry III orders the death of Henry de Guisa at Blois. Carlos de Mayenne collects his leadership and the war enters his final phase.
Henry III was killed after his association with Henry of Navarre with his League. Valois- Angula line was killed and Henry of Navarre claims his crown as Henry IV.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski are putting together mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

eventos.titulo: Polish, imperial and German princes meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins forces from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes over the command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgns, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

people.KESTUTISLIT: Prince of Trakai and chief of the Western defence under Algirdas. He briefly removed Jogaila and was a great duke in 1381-1382. He died captive in Kreva; he was the father of Vitauts the Great.
people.SKIRGAILALIT: Brother and collaborator of Jogaila, was his lieutenant in Lithuania until the Astrava agreement of 1392. He then received land in Volinia and the Kyiv principality; his delegated office differs from the sovereignty of the grand duke.
people.SVITRIGAILALIT: It happened to Vitauts in 1430 and lost Vilna in the 1432 coup. A civil war continued with support from eastern provinces; after the defeats of 1435-1438, it retained its own signory trajectory in Volinia.
people.ZYGIMANTASLIT: Son of Kęstutis and brother of Vitauts, he joined the government in 1432. He beat Švitrigaila in the civil war and was killed in Trakai in 1440.
people.JANZAMOYSKI: Chancellor and Grand Hetman of the Polish Crown, adviser to Stephen Báthory and a central figure in Commonwealth politics. He founded Zamość and its academy, combining military command, parliamentary activity and humanist patronage.
people.JANAMORTARNOWSKI: Grand Crown Hetman who organised campaigns against Moldavia and Muscovy. His house combined military service, political influence and extensive estates in Lesser Poland.
people.JANKRZTARNOWSKI: The son of Hetman Jan Amor Tarnowski served as royal secretary and Castellan of Wojnicz. His death left the family inheritance to his sister Zofia.
people.ZOFIATARNOWSKA: Jan Amor Tarnowski’s daughter and the wife of Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski. After her brother Jan Krzysztof’s death, her inheritance connected Tarnów with the Ostrogski estates.
people.FIODORSANGUSZKO: A prince of the Nesuchoje and Łokacze branch, he served as Marshal of Volhynia and as a starosta. His sons Roman and Dymitr took part in the military and political life of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
people.ROMANSANGUSZKO: A Lithuanian prince and commander who fought in the Livonian War and held the voivodeship of Bracław. He took part in the negotiations leading to the Union of Lublin.
people.DYMITRSANGUSZKO: Fiodor Sanguszko’s son and Roman’s brother. His marriage to Halszka Ostrogska provoked a conflict over the young woman’s guardianship and inheritance.
people.KAZIMIERZCZARTORYSKI: Prince of Klewań and Żuków and Castellan of Vilnius. His children Michał Fryderyk, August Aleksander and Konstancja belonged to the generation that strengthened Czartoryski political influence.
people.MICHALCZARTORYSKI: Grand Chancellor of Lithuania and a leader of the Familia, the political grouping centred on the Czartoryskis. His activity combined institutional reform and alliances between magnates.
people.AUGUSTCZARTORYSKI: Voivode of Ruthenia and a leading figure in the Familia. His marriage to Maria Zofia Sieniawska expanded the Czartoryskis’ landed and political resources.
people.TADEUSZKOSCIUSZKO: A military engineer and general of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. He fought in the American Revolution and led the uprising of 1794 against foreign intervention and the partition of his country.

eventos.titulo: The Union of Lublin creates the Community
eventos.descripcion: Poland and Lithuania move from a dynastic union to a closer political community. The new structure will survive the male extinction of the Jagellones and will make a common elected monarchy possible.
Following the death without heirs of Segismundo II Augusto, the nobility chose Henry of Valois and set his true power with his final limits through his Henricians.

eventos.titulo: Ana Jagellón and Stephen Báthory share the crown
eventos.descripcion: The choice of Stephen Báthory with Ana Jagellón shows that the dynastic legitimacy still matters, but it is no longer enough on its own: the crown depends on the choice of nobility.

eventos.titulo: A Vasa is elected King of Poland
eventos.descripcion: Segismundo III Vasa arrives at the Polish-Lithuanian crown as grandson of Segismundo I and Swedish prince. The election opens up a stage at which the Communidad intersects directly with the dynastic struggles of the Baltic.
After decades of wars and crises, John II Casimir abandons his throne. Nobility can re-choose from scratch and leapt for a candidate born within his own Commonwealth.

eventos.titulo: The Battle and Relief of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, habeburgic and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman site of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens up a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Augusto the Strong gets the crown
eventos.descripcion: The election of Saxony becomes Catholicism and is able to be elected king. Poland - Lithuania is personally united with Saxony and its choice makes the crown a European issue.
Estanislao Leszczyński and Augusto III are proclaimed by rival factions. The dispute leads to a European war and shows how far the neighbouring powers can condition electoral freedom.

eventos.titulo: The Last King of the Republic
eventos.descripcion: Estanislao Augusto poniatowski is elected king with a reformist program but under Russia's decisive shadow. The tension between noble freedom, reform and outside intervention enters its final phase.

eventos.titulo: The May 3 Constitution tries to change the system
eventos.descripcion: The new constitution eliminates the liberum veto and replaces the elective monarchy with an hereditary succession envisaged in the house of Saxony. It is the most ambitious attempt to reform the Republic from within.

eventos.titulo: The third partition ends with the Commonwealth
eventos.descripcion: The third partition erases the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the political map and forces Estanislao Augusto to abdicate. The chosen crown experiment concludes under pressure from the neighbouring monarchies.
Luis de Condé dies after the battle of Jarnac. Gaspar de Coligny remains as the leading military boss of the town while Duke of Anjou, future Henry III, gain prestige in the Catholic field.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Paris RetiN up for the League
eventos.descripcion: The Day of Barricades forces Henry III to leave Paris and shows that the League and Henry of Guisa can directly challenge the king in his own capital.

eventos.titulo: Henry III killed the Duke of Guisa
eventos.descripcion: Fearing to lose control of the monarchy, Henry III orders the death of Henry de Guisa at Blois. Carlos de Mayenne collects his leadership and the war enters his final phase.
Henry III was killed after his association with Henry of Navarre with his League. Valois- Angula line was killed and Henry of Navarre claims his crown as Henry IV.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski are putting together mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

eventos.titulo: Polish, imperial and German princes meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins forces from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes over the command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgns, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

people.STAN1LESZ: King elected from Poland on two occasions and father-in-law of Louis XV of France. After losing the crown, Lorraine received a remarkable, illustrated cut.
people.STANPONFATHER: Noble of the House of Poniatowski. Their life was connected with Poland.
people.KONSTCZART: Noble of the House of Czartoryski. Their life was connected with Poland, Lithuania.
people.STAN2PONIAT: He attempted to reform the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth under intense foreign pressure. The partitions and the defeat of constitutional projects brought his monarchy to an end.
people.ANNAPOLPOM: Consort of the House of Jagiellon. Their life was connected with Poland, Pomerania.
people.GEORGE2RAKOCZI: He tried to conquer the Polish crown without Ottoman authorization. The failure of the 1657 campaign led to punishment, invasions and quarrels over the throne that disbanded much of his father's inherited stability.
people.JANZAMOYSKI: Chancellor and Grand Hetman of the Polish Crown, adviser to Stephen Báthory and a central figure in Commonwealth politics. He founded Zamość and its academy, combining military command, parliamentary activity and humanist patronage.
people.JANAMORTARNOWSKI: Grand Crown Hetman who organised campaigns against Moldavia and Muscovy. His house combined military service, political influence and extensive estates in Lesser Poland.
people.JANKRZTARNOWSKI: The son of Hetman Jan Amor Tarnowski served as royal secretary and Castellan of Wojnicz. His death left the family inheritance to his sister Zofia.
people.ZOFIATARNOWSKA: Jan Amor Tarnowski’s daughter and the wife of Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski. After her brother Jan Krzysztof’s death, her inheritance connected Tarnów with the Ostrogski estates.
people.FIODORSANGUSZKO: A prince of the Nesuchoje and Łokacze branch, he served as Marshal of Volhynia and as a starosta. His sons Roman and Dymitr took part in the military and political life of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
people.ROMANSANGUSZKO: A Lithuanian prince and commander who fought in the Livonian War and held the voivodeship of Bracław. He took part in the negotiations leading to the Union of Lublin.
people.DYMITRSANGUSZKO: Fiodor Sanguszko’s son and Roman’s brother. His marriage to Halszka Ostrogska provoked a conflict over the young woman’s guardianship and inheritance.
people.KAZIMIERZCZARTORYSKI: Prince of Klewań and Żuków and Castellan of Vilnius. His children Michał Fryderyk, August Aleksander and Konstancja belonged to the generation that strengthened Czartoryski political influence.
people.MICHALCZARTORYSKI: Grand Chancellor of Lithuania and a leader of the Familia, the political grouping centred on the Czartoryskis. His activity combined institutional reform and alliances between magnates.
people.AUGUSTCZARTORYSKI: Voivode of Ruthenia and a leading figure in the Familia. His marriage to Maria Zofia Sieniawska expanded the Czartoryskis’ landed and political resources.
people.TADEUSZKOSCIUSZKO: A military engineer and general of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. He fought in the American Revolution and led the uprising of 1794 against foreign intervention and the partition of his country.

name: Trinacria
summary: This entry follows the island crown after the Sicilian Vespers. The Sicilians accepted Peter III but opposed James II’s renunciation and elected Frederick. Caltabellotta offered a conditional peace, not a definitive separation: the transmission to Peter II and the successions of Louis, Frederick and Maria kept the question open.

notes.Denominación usada aquí para seguir la c: Name used here to follow the insular crown from 1282. The title of Trinacria was formalised with Caltabellotta and the papal ratification of 1303 and was not the unique name of the island from the beginning.

evolucion.texto: Peter III intervenes after the Sicilian Vespers.
James II’s renunciation at Anagni is rejected in Sicily.
Frederick is crowned in Palermo.
Caltabellotta recognises his rule for life; the title is ratified in 1303.
Frederick associates Peter with the throne, contrary to the peace settlement’s succession terms.
The Avignon agreement redefines relations with Naples and the papacy.
Maria inherits while still a minor.
Maria and Martin establish themselves on the island with Aragonese support.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel de Castilla and Fernando de Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberic peninsula without legalizing them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada before Elizabeth I and Ferdinand II puts an end to the Nasrid emirate, Muhammad XII, Boabdil, and his town.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States, defeats the Ottoman army of Ali Bajá after hours of combat of galera against galera. The Ottoman center is falling apart, Uluç Ali is able to save part of its wing and thousands of combatants are killed, injured or held captive. The victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but it destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic victory of the coalition.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of the Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Benevent: The Anjou take the kingdom
eventos.descripcion: Carlos de Anjou, backed by the papacy, defeats and kills Manfredo in Benevento. The Hohenstaufen monarchy loses effective control of Sicily and Naples.
Conradino invades Italy to recover his family's inheritance, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou is left as the owner of the old Hohenstaufen kingdom.
After years of war, the Sicians hold up Federico, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line opposite the Andean Naples.

The peace of Caltabelletta recognizes Frederick on the island and the Anjou on mainland. The old Sicilian monarchy remains politically broken between Trinacria and the kingdom that historiography will call Naples.

Alfonso V. of Aragon defeates the angevine resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since the Visperas, an same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the mainland kingdom, though the crowns have separate identities.

eventos.titulo: The inheritance of Alfonso once again secures
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to his brother John II while Naples remains for his son Fernando. The personal union does not become a stable fusion of the crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Fernando the Catholic agree to share with themselves the kingdom of Federico I. The cooperation lasts for little: the challenges about the boundaries of partition turn old allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Grand Captain challenges the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms strengthens the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance that was born from the 1500 division was definitely broken in favor of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Fernando gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Fernando the Catholic as King of Naples and Trinacria. The two parts of the old Sicilian monarchy share again sovereign, but will continue to be administered as different kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

In Mesina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetian, pontificas, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.

In the center, the Royal Galera of Don Juan and the Sultana of Ali Bajá are stuck in a struggle of approaches, archauces and successive reinforcements. The fall of Ali Bajá and the take of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic core of victory.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to leave his Sicilian purport at Anagni, but the Sicilian did not accept to come back to Angevin rule. They chose his brother Federico and forced the Casa de Barcelona to divide about his future.

Caltabellotta had been planning to put up with his life and a later solution to the Anjou. To associate Peter with his throne, the island house defended his own hereditary transmission. The peace of 1302 had been closed.

eventos.titulo: A new peace redefines the two Sicilia
eventos.descripcion: The papal mediation gave a new framework to Federico's recognition as King of Trinacria with obligations to Juana. The names of Sicily and Trinacria expressed rights discussed as well as a geographical separation.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to put their arms at the Barons. The Queen's hereditary legitimacy was insufficient without his military capacity. The island's government again closely linked with the Aragon's Crown.

name: Scotland
summary: Scotland maintained an independent crown throughout the Middle Ages and much of the early modern period. James VI’s succession in England created a personal union; political union came later.

uniones.resumen: James VI of Scotland became his first and second The dynastic union preceded parliamentary union in more than a century.
uniones.instituciones: The two kingdoms have preserved parliaments and legal systems. The crisis and the Republican period of 1649-1660 have been an end to the monarchy and 1707 have created a different political framework.

etapas.texto: James happened to Elizabeth I without merging the institutions of both kingdoms.

personas.resumen: James VI of Scotland and I of England joined in his person the English and Scottish crowns in 1603. His reign opened the stage of the Estudo in England.

etapas.texto: The performance of Charles I opened up the Republican period in England and Scotland first followed another path to his military submission.
The monarchy reunited both kingdoms under Charles II.
The acts of union created the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Scottish legal system maintained its identity.

persona.resumen: King of Scotland for almost half a century. His long reign links the 12th century monarchy with the succession of Alexander II.
Son of William the Lion. He reigned from 1214 to 1249 and consolidated the Anglo-Scottish border before dying during a campaign in the west.
His accidental death in 1286 left the Scottish monarchy without a direct adult heir and opened the great successor crisis of the late 13th century.
Alexander III's granddaughter and recognized heiress of the Scottish crown. He died in 1290 during the trip to Scotland, triggering the succession dispute known as the Great Cause.
Elected king in 1292 after the arbitration of Edward I of England in the Great Cause. It was deposed in 1296 at the beginning of the open phase of the wars of independence.
King of Scotland since 1306. After years of war against England, his victory in Bannokburn in 1314 consolidated the recovery of the Scottish independent monarchy.
The son of Robert I Bruce, king of Scotland since 1329. He spent years in exile in France and 11 captive in England after being defeated in Neville's Cross (1346).
Son of King John Balliol, claimed the Scottish throne with English support in front of David II. It was crowned in 1332, but never consolidated its authority and resigned in 1356.
Son of Marjorie Bruce and Walter Stewart. In 1371 he became the first king of Stewart's House.
King of Scotland since 1390, son of Robert II. For his poor health, the government was exercised by his brother, the Duke of Albany, and his son David, who died in custody in 1402.
King of Scotland since 1406, spent 18 years captive in England. On his return he strengthened the real authority in front of the nobility and was killed in Perth in 1437.
King of Scotland from 1437, at age six. He ended the Douglas's power and died in 1460 when a cannon exploded during the siege of Roxburgh.
King of Scotland since 1460. He incorporated the Orcades and the Shetland for his marriage to Margarita of Denmark and died after the battle of Sauchieburn (1488) against noble rebels.
He strengthened the Scottish court and navy and maintained the alliance with France. He died in Flodden, a defeat that left another regal minority in Scotland.
He sought to affirm his authority in front of the nobility and maintained the French alliance. His death left the crown to Mary Estuardo when he had only a few days of life.

Queen of Scotland from childhood and Queen consort of France for her marriage to Francis II. His life was marked by religious struggles, the Scottish nobility crisis and his dynastic rivalry with Elizabeth I.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel de Castilla and Fernando de Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberic peninsula without legalizing them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada before Elizabeth I and Ferdinand II puts an end to the Nasrid emirate, Muhammad XII, Boabdil, and his town.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
After years of war, the Sicians hold up Federico, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line opposite the Andean Naples.

Alfonso V. of Aragon defeates the angevine resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since the Visperas, an same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the mainland kingdom, though the crowns have separate identities.

eventos.titulo: The inheritance of Alfonso once again secures
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to his brother John II while Naples remains for his son Fernando. The personal union does not become a stable fusion of the crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Fernando the Catholic agree to share with themselves the kingdom of Federico I. The cooperation lasts for little: the challenges about the boundaries of partition turn old allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Grand Captain challenges the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms strengthens the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance that was born from the 1500 division was definitely broken in favor of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Fernando gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Fernando the Catholic as King of Naples and Trinacria. The two parts of the old Sicilian monarchy share again sovereign, but will continue to be administered as different kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to leave his Sicilian purport at Anagni, but the Sicilian did not accept to come back to Angevin rule. They chose his brother Federico and forced the Casa de Barcelona to divide about his future.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to put their arms at the Barons. The Queen's hereditary legitimacy was insufficient without his military capacity. The island's government again closely linked with the Aragon's Crown.

name: Cilician Armenia
summary: The Cilician monarchy emerged from an Armenian principality in the north-eastern Mediterranean. Marriages among the Rubenids, Hethumids and Lusignans connected it with Antioch, Cyprus and Byzantium. Its search for Mongol and Western assistance did not prevent its fall to the Mamluks. name: Brittany
summary: Brittany retained its own ducal tradition and considerable autonomy between the French and English crowns. The marriage of Alix of Thouars and Peter of Dreux established a Capetian branch in the duchy. John III’s childless death opened a dispute in 1341 between his niece Joan of Penthièvre and his half-brother John of Montfort, whose claims followed different family lines. After the Montfort victory, succession passed among brothers, uncles and cousins until Francis II and his daughter Anne. The marriages of Anne and her daughter Claude linked the duchy with the French monarchy; the institutional union of 1532 was a later step that preserved distinct privileges.

eventos.titulo: The symbolic beginning of the Lutheran Reform
eventos.descripcion: The dispute over indulgences makes Martin Luther the center of a dispute that soon overcomes academic debate and questions authority, doctrine and obedience.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Reformist princes and cities protest against the reversal of religious concessions. The name that will end up identifying the Protestant churches is born from this political protest.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.

name: Granada
summary: The Nasrid Emirate was the last major Islamic polity on the Iberian Peninsula. It alternated diplomacy, tribute and war with Castile, while internal conflicts sometimes fragmented power.

notes.El emirato nazarí se representa mediante: The Nasrid emirate is represented by the aggregated regions of Málaga, Almería and Granada. Málaga passed to Castile in 1487, Almería in 1489 and Granada in 1492 and each SVG region also contains areas with more complex local trajectory.

persona.resumen: Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the County of Burgundy, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He then incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groninga and Guelders in a step-by-step manner between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535, Milan has been under imperial control; Philip II's invasion and subsequent possession must be distinguished from that government.

eventos.descripcion: Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Papal States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

summary: Hum, or Zahumlje, was a historical region with its own princes and lords, connected at different times with Serbian, Hungarian and Bosnian powers. Conquest by a sovereign or administration by a lord did not erase its identity. Its western and eastern parts did not always follow the same political course.

notes.Hum/Zahumlje: principado medieval y seño: Hum/Zahumlje was a medieval principality and lordship subject to changing local powers and overlordships. A change of lord does not create a new territory; lordly mandates and mapped areas are dated separately.

persona.nombre: Philip of Valois, Duke of Orléans
persona.resumen: The minor son of Philip VI of France and Joan of Burgundy, received in 1344 the duchy of Orleans. He fought at Poitiers (1356) and was held hostage in England after the treaty of Brétigny and died in 1375 with no legitimate children.
Charles VI's disease made him one of the great competitors for the control of the French monarchy. His murder on the orders of Juan without Fear aggravated the war between armagnacs and Burgundianes.
He was captured in Agincourt and spent many years in England. His poetic work made him a prominent figure in French courtesan literature.
Brother of Louis XIII, he participated in several conspirations against Richelieu and real politics. His position as a possible heir gave him influence until the birth of the future Louis XIV.
Brother of Louis XIV, founded the modern branch of Orleans. He combined a subordinate position in the court with a prominent military participation, especially in Cassel.

eventos.titulo: Henry III killed the Duke of Guisa
eventos.descripcion: Fearing to lose control of the monarchy, Henry III orders the death of Henry de Guisa at Blois. Carlos de Mayenne collects his leadership and the war enters his final phase.
